brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
Manipuri tea, also called Kanglei tea, is a black tea grown in the northeastern Indian state of Manipur. Its leaves are reportedly twisted and curled by hand.

Treat it as you would any black tea: water just off the boil, a few minutes in the pot, and a seller who can say where it was grown.
history: The tea industry in Manipur remains small, and state support for small growers has made the tea easier to find in recent years. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Described as an orthodox black tea whose leaves are twisted and curled by hand after withering rather than rolled in the usual way.
harvest_season: Picked through the growing season, as with most black teas.
taste_profile: A slightly floral aroma is reported.
vintage_note: Black teas are normally sold by harvest year and are best within a couple of years.
